blocks.text: Why does the internal energy of an ideal gas remain constant during isothermal expansion?

Thus, if the gas expands and does external work, it is done at the expense of the internal energy of its molecules and, hence, the temperature of the gas falls. Conversely, an adiabatic compression causes the temperature of the gas to rise because of the work done on the gas.
Adiabatic change occurs when the gas expands or is compressed rapidly, particularly when the gas is contained in an insulated cylinder. The examples of adiabatic processes are:

items: The rapid escape of air from a burst tyre.
The rapid expansion and compression of air through which a sound wave is passing.
